note: Decision board. Each suggestion lists the options, a recommendation and the evidence. NOTHING here is implemented until the owner records a choice in the `decision` field (or tells the agent the IDs). Recommendations are judgments built on the cited official sources; they are not program facts. Suggestions that depend on a missing answer name the question IDs in `needs_answers` (see ledger/questions.json).

suggestions.title: Launch the public site before, or after, the Associates account is approved?
suggestions.suggestion: Publish the research pages now, but add no live affiliate links until an Associates account is approved and Special Links are generated for it.
suggestions.why: Amazon requires at least three qualifying sales within 180 days before the application is reviewed, and personal orders do not count. Special Links must use the assigned Associates ID. The supplied short links carry per-link btn_ref tokens, not an Associate tag (F-24).

options.label: Research-only launch; links added after approval
options.tradeoff: Safest. No affiliate revenue at launch and no compliance exposure from untagged links.

options.label: Launch with the supplied short links now
options.tradeoff: Not recommended. Short links are not Special Links with the owner's Associates ID, and the owner's tag is not on them (F-24).

options.label: Launch with placeholder tagged links that switch on after approval
options.tradeoff: Workable, but the placeholder must never resolve to a live affiliate link before approval.

suggestions.title: Which products and how wide a niche?
suggestions.suggestion: Start with the three supplied air-fryer products as one comparison set. Widen to a niche only after authorised demand data is connected.
suggestions.why: The three destination pages are all air fryers or air-fryer ovens and share the breadcrumb Home & Kitchen › Kitchen & Dining › Small Appliances › Fryers › Air Fryers (S19–S21). No authorised demand or sales-rank data is connected (ledger niches.json).

options.label: The three supplied products only
options.tradeoff: Smallest verified scope. Narrow search demand; can grow later.

options.label: Countertop air fryers and air-fryer ovens
options.tradeoff: Larger scope, needs search and sales data that is not yet connected. Creators API search needs 10 qualifying sales in 30 days (S07).

options.label: Broad home kitchen
options.tradeoff: Not recommended now. Many unrelated categories; no evidence yet for any of them.

suggestions.title: Keep a pricing module at all?
suggestions.suggestion: Remove price tracking and price alerts from the product scope. Show price only when Amazon serves it on the link or when a dated Creators API response supports it.
suggestions.why: Participation Requirements Section 6(y): the site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality unless Amazon agrees otherwise (ledger R-22). Price and availability may only be shown under the conditions in R-04.

options.label: Drop price tracking and alerts from scope
options.tradeoff: Compliant by default. Loses a feature the original brief named.

options.label: Keep static, dated price snapshots from the Creators API only
options.tradeoff: Needs API eligibility (Q-02), and still must not track or alert on price.

options.label: Ask Amazon for written agreement first
options.tradeoff: Only route to a tracking feature. Timing and outcome unknown.

suggestions.title: Which article formats go first?
suggestions.suggestion: Lead with evergreen buying guides and a how-to format that makes no product claims. Add product comparisons only when every spec in them has an official source.
suggestions.why: Trend and demand data are not connected, so no topic can be called trending on evidence. Product claims must be accurate and not misleading (R-06, R-21).

options.label: Buying guide: air fryer vs air-fryer oven for a household
options.tradeoff: Evergreen. Needs spec sources for each product.

options.label: Head-to-head comparison of the three products
options.tradeoff: Strongest buyer intent. Blocked until the three ASINs and specs are confirmed (Q-03).

options.label: How-to articles (cooking method, cleaning, safety) with no product claims
options.tradeoff: Lowest compliance risk. Weaker direct commission link.

suggestions.title: Can the site say the products were tested?
suggestions.suggestion: Use data-led wording only ("the manufacturer lists…", "the destination page shows…") until a person has used the products and kept dated test notes.
suggestions.why: Claims that a product was used or tested are only allowed when true, and the repo has no test records. Unsupported claims fall under R-06 and R-21.

options.label: Data-led wording only
options.tradeoff: Honest and compliant. Reads less personal.

options.label: Hands-on reviews with dated test notes
options.tradeoff: Best editorial value. Requires a real tester and logged results (Q-11).

options.label: Both, labelled per article
options.tradeoff: Flexible. Each article must state which kind it is.

suggestions.recommended: A now; B or C only with test records

suggestions.title: What should the public site look like?
suggestions.suggestion: Make the public site an editorial guide (long-form pages, real data tables, visible sources and an updated date). Keep the dashboard for the owner's review. Use Amazon product images only if Q-10 is cleared.
suggestions.why: The brief asks for a polished marketing site that does not read like generic AI output. Concrete signals that help: a named editor, visible sources, dated updates, and no unsourced superlatives. Image use is limited by Program Content rules (R-31).

options.label: Editorial magazine style for public pages; dashboard for owner
options.tradeoff: Matches the brief. Two visual systems to maintain.

options.label: One dashboard-style look everywhere
options.tradeoff: Simplest. Reads more like a tool than a marketing site.

options.label: Minimal product-guide look
options.tradeoff: Clean and fast. Less distinctive.

suggestions.title: Show star ratings and review counts?
suggestions.suggestion: Show none until API-sourced data is available, then show only what the API returns, with its date.
suggestions.why: Participation Requirements Section 6(t): reviews and star ratings may not be displayed unless obtained through the Creators API or PA-API. The Creators API needs 10 qualifying sales in 30 days (S07).

options.label: No ratings or review counts
options.tradeoff: Compliant. Loses a common trust signal.

options.label: API-sourced ratings with date stamp, after eligibility
options.tradeoff: Best trust signal. Depends on Q-02.

suggestions.title: Which commission band should the revenue model use?
suggestions.suggestion: Model revenue with a range that covers the candidate Table 1 bands, and mark the chosen band as unconfirmed until Amazon's category for each ASIN is confirmed.
suggestions.why: Table 1 lists Kitchen at 4.50% and Home at 3.00%; the All Other default is 4.00% (S04). The destination breadcrumb reads Home & Kitchen, which does not by itself name the Table 1 band. Commission is paid only on qualifying purchases and is never guaranteed (R-19).

options.label: Range from 3.00% to 4.50%, band unconfirmed
options.tradeoff: Honest. Wider range; no single headline number.

options.label: Use Kitchen 4.50% as the planning value
options.tradeoff: Plausible but unconfirmed for these ASINs. Would overstate income if the band differs.

options.label: Wait for Amazon's confirmation before modelling
options.tradeoff: Most accurate. Delays the revenue model.

suggestions.title: How should clicks and conversions be tracked?
suggestions.suggestion: Use static campaign keys per page (sub-tags that never identify a visitor), and rely on Amazon's Associates reports for conversions.
suggestions.why: Sub-tags may monitor and optimise Special Links but must not be tied to an individual user (R-08). Associates reports are an official tool (S09).

options.label: Per-page static sub-tags plus Associates reports
options.tradeoff: Compliant and simple. Coarse, page-level data only.

options.label: Associates reports only
options.tradeoff: Simplest. No per-page breakdown.

options.label: Site analytics on top of A
options.tradeoff: More insight. Needs a privacy and consent review before it is added (not researched here).

suggestions.title: How are approved suggestions implemented?
suggestions.suggestion: Implement only what the owner has marked in the decision field, one batch at a time, each with its own commit and a rebuilt, checked site.
suggestions.why: The brief asks for a review step before any change. Batching keeps each change traceable to a recorded decision. The source (S22) is only the publishing mechanism: the live site is served by GitHub Pages, so each approved batch goes live on the Pages build.

options.label: Owner marks each decision; agent implements that batch
options.tradeoff: Clear audit trail. Needs the owner to respond.

options.label: Owner approves in one pass per week
options.tradeoff: Fewer rounds. Larger batches.

options.label: Agent implements low-risk items without asking
options.tradeoff: Not recommended for anything that touches compliance or money.

suggestions.title: Close the 'at least 10 posts' content bar before applying, rather than after
suggestions.suggestion: Treat Amazon's content bar as a build gate: publish editorial posts that are a reason to visit the site on their own, and only then apply. Each post carries the same source discipline as the rest of this repository: a named demand question, at least one value read from an official page with its link, and no claim of hands-on use.
suggestions.why: S23 states that all Sites must have robust original content, that 'a good rule of thumb is at least 10 posts', that content must be recent, and that an application is rejected for unoriginal or insufficient content. The repository publishes 14 counted editorial pages (see release/index.html RR-03), but they are specification and comparison surfaces: each one is written to answer a question about these three listings, not to be found by a search. Amazon rejects and does not reassess, so the work has to happen before the application, not after it is refused.

options.label: Gate the application: no application until 10 posts pass the same source check as the rest of the site
options.tradeoff: Slowest to revenue, and the only option that cannot be refused for content. Needs the owner's author identity (Q-16) before a byline can be honest.

options.label: Apply now and add posts during the 180-day review window
options.tradeoff: S23 says the team reviews once qualifying sales arrive, so there is a window. Risky: S23 states a rejected application is not reassessed, so a rejection at the wrong moment is permanent.

options.label: Publish the posts but do not apply until the owner has a domain (Q-17)
options.tradeoff: Removes the ownership question from the same review, at the cost of a second delay.
